description: This topic covers writing application letters, CVs and speeches, and the skills of analysing, reading a variety of, commenting on the usefulness of, and composing functional texts for real-world purposes and audiences.

mcq.questionText: An application letter for a job vacancy should typically begin by:

options.text: Stating the position being applied for and where it was advertised

mcq.explanation: An effective application letter opens by clearly stating which position is being applied for and how the applicant learned of it. Exam Tip: Clarity from the very first line helps the reader immediately understand the letter's purpose.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following is an appropriate closing phrase for an application letter?

options.text: "I look forward to the opportunity of an interview."

mcq.explanation: This closing phrase is professional and expresses genuine interest in proceeding to the next stage of the hiring process. Exam Tip: Application letters should close formally and positively, restating interest in the position.

mcq.questionText: A CV (Curriculum Vitae) typically includes which of the following sections?

options.text: Personal details, education, work experience and skills

mcq.explanation: A CV is a structured summary of a person's education, work experience, skills and relevant personal details. Exam Tip: CVs should be clear, organised and factual — not written as a narrative or story.

mcq.questionText: A speech written to be delivered at a graduation ceremony is an example of a functional text because it:

options.text: Serves a specific real-world purpose and audience, such as celebrating and advising graduates
Is purely for entertainment with no purpose
Cannot be written down in advance

mcq.explanation: Functional texts serve a specific, practical, real-world communicative purpose, and a graduation speech is written for this exact purpose. Exam Tip: Functional texts are defined by their real-world PURPOSE, not by their format alone.

mcq.questionText: Which of these is an example of a functional text?

options.text: A user manual for a phone

mcq.explanation: A user manual serves a clear, practical purpose — instructing the reader on how to use a product — making it a functional text. Exam Tip: Functional texts include manuals, recipes, brochures, application letters, CVs, and similar practical documents.

mcq.questionText: Analysing a brochure for a local hospital by examining its purpose, content, organisation and design demonstrates:
mcq.explanation: This demonstrates the specific skill of analysing a functional text across its key dimensions: purpose, content, organisation and design. Exam Tip: A complete functional text analysis considers WHY it exists, WHAT it says, HOW it is organised, and its visual DESIGN.

mcq.questionText: Reading a recipe, a bus timetable and a product warranty card in a single lesson demonstrates:

options.text: Reading a variety of functional texts

mcq.explanation: This demonstrates engaging with several different types of functional (practical, purpose-driven) texts within one learning activity. Exam Tip: Functional texts vary widely in format, from recipes to timetables to official documents.

mcq.questionText: Evaluating whether a school's noticeboard poster effectively communicates an upcoming event demonstrates:

options.text: Commenting on the usefulness of a functional text
Composing a completely new poster with no reference to the original

mcq.explanation: This demonstrates critically assessing how well a functional text achieves its intended communicative purpose. Exam Tip: Usefulness is judged by how effectively a text achieves its specific, practical purpose for its intended audience.

mcq.questionText: Writing a set of clear instructions for operating a classroom projector demonstrates:
mcq.explanation: Writing clear, practical instructions for a specific purpose (operating equipment) demonstrates composing a functional text. Exam Tip: Functional texts should be composed with the intended reader's practical needs clearly in mind.

mcq.questionText: Which of these best demonstrates an appropriate structure for a job application letter?

options.text: A single, unstructured paragraph with no greeting or closing
A formal greeting, an opening stating the position applied for, a body highlighting relevant qualifications/experience, and a formal closing
A poem describing the applicant's feelings

mcq.explanation: A well-structured application letter follows a clear formal format: greeting, purpose statement, relevant qualifications, and formal closing. Exam Tip: Structure and formality both matter significantly in professional application letters.

mcq.questionText: Which detail would typically NOT belong in a CV?

options.text: A detailed account of a childhood holiday with no relevance to skills or experience

mcq.explanation: A CV should focus on relevant, professional information; an unrelated childhood holiday account does not serve the CV's practical purpose. Exam Tip: Every detail in a CV should be relevant to demonstrating suitability for a role or opportunity.

mcq.questionText: A speech prepared for a wedding ceremony, thanking guests and offering well-wishes to the couple, is an example of:

options.text: A functional text serving a specific ceremonial purpose

mcq.explanation: This speech serves a specific real-world social purpose (a wedding celebration), making it a functional text. Exam Tip: Functional texts appear across many real-life situations, not only in business or school contexts.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following best demonstrates commenting on the usefulness of a bus timetable as a functional text?

options.text: Ignoring whether the timetable is accurate or clear
Noting whether the timetable's departure times are clearly organised and easy for passengers to find quickly
Rewriting the timetable as a poem
Assuming all timetables are equally useful regardless of design

mcq.explanation: Commenting on usefulness means specifically evaluating how well the text serves its practical purpose for its intended users. Exam Tip: A timetable's usefulness depends heavily on clarity and ease of finding relevant information quickly.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following texts would require analysis of its "design" as part of a full functional text analysis?

options.text: A private, handwritten diary entry never meant to be seen by others
A public health poster warning about a disease outbreak, which uses bold colours and images to attract attention
A single word written on a napkin

mcq.explanation: A public health poster's visual design (colours, images, layout) plays a genuine role in how effectively its message reaches and impacts its audience. Exam Tip: Design matters especially for visually-oriented functional texts like posters, brochures and advertisements.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following best demonstrates composing an appropriate application letter for a shop assistant vacancy?

options.text: A letter demanding immediate employment with no reference to qualifications
A letter stating the position applied for, briefly outlining relevant experience with customers or sales, and requesting an interview
A letter describing an unrelated personal problem
A letter written entirely in the third person about someone else

mcq.explanation: An effective application letter clearly states the position, highlights genuinely relevant experience, and requests further engagement (an interview). Exam Tip: Relevance is key — only include experience or skills that support your suitability for the specific role.

fib.questionText: A letter written to formally apply for a job vacancy is called an ________ letter.
fib.explanation: This letter type formally requests consideration for a specific job or opportunity. Exam Tip: Application letters should be clear, formal, and focused on relevant qualifications.

fib.questionText: A document summarising a person's education, work experience and skills, typically submitted alongside a job application, is called a ________.
fib.explanation: This document type gives a structured overview of a person's professional background. Exam Tip: CV stands for Curriculum Vitae, meaning "course of life" in Latin.

fib.questionText: A speech written specifically for a real-world occasion such as a graduation or wedding is an example of a ________ text.
fib.explanation: This term describes a text serving a specific, practical, real-world communicative purpose. Exam Tip: Functional texts serve real purposes for real audiences, unlike purely creative or fictional writing.

fib.questionText: Examining a functional text's purpose, content, organisation and design is called ________ a functional text.
fib.explanation: This term describes the process of critically examining these key dimensions of a functional text. Exam Tip: A thorough analysis considers WHY, WHAT, HOW (organisation) and visual DESIGN together.

fib.questionText: Engaging with recipes, timetables, manuals and other practical texts is called reading a ________ of functional texts.
fib.explanation: This term describes exposure to and engagement with different types of practical, purpose-driven texts. Exam Tip: Functional texts vary widely — recipes, manuals, brochures, timetables, and more.

fib.questionText: Evaluating how well a functional text achieves its intended communicative purpose is called commenting on its ________.
fib.explanation: This term describes assessing how effectively a text serves its practical, real-world purpose. Exam Tip: Usefulness is judged relative to the text's intended audience and purpose.

fib.questionText: Writing a clear set of instructions or a new brochure for a specific practical purpose is called ________ a functional text.
fib.explanation: This term describes actively creating a new functional text for a genuine, practical purpose. Exam Tip: Composing functional texts requires keeping the intended reader's practical needs clearly in mind.

fib.questionText: Complete the appropriate opening of an application letter: "I am writing to apply for the position of ________ advertised in your notice."

options.text: the name of the vacant position

fib.explanation: This phrase clearly states the specific position being applied for, right at the start of the letter. Exam Tip: Clearly naming the position avoids any confusion about the letter's purpose.

fib.questionText: A CV typically includes sections for personal details, ________, work experience and skills.
fib.explanation: This section lists the applicant's academic qualifications and schooling history. Exam Tip: Education details are usually listed in reverse chronological order (most recent first).

fib.questionText: A public health poster's visual design, including colours and images, is analysed as part of examining a functional text's ________.
fib.explanation: This term describes the visual, layout-related aspect of a functional text. Exam Tip: Design particularly matters for visually-oriented functional texts like posters and brochures.

tf.questionText: An application letter should clearly state the position being applied for.
tf.explanation: This matches the standard, essential requirement for a clear, effective application letter. Exam Tip: Clarity about the position avoids confusion for the reader/employer.

tf.questionText: A CV should include a detailed, unrelated personal story with no connection to skills or experience.
tf.explanation: A CV should focus on RELEVANT professional information; an unrelated personal story does not serve its practical purpose. Exam Tip: Every CV detail should demonstrate suitability for a role or opportunity.

tf.questionText: A wedding speech can be considered a functional text because it serves a specific real-world social purpose.
tf.explanation: This matches the broader definition of functional texts as serving genuine, practical, real-world purposes, including social/ceremonial ones. Exam Tip: Functional texts are not limited to business or school contexts.

tf.questionText: Analysing a functional text's design is irrelevant and should always be skipped.
tf.explanation: Analysing design IS relevant, especially for visually-oriented functional texts like posters and brochures, where design affects communicative effectiveness. Exam Tip: Purpose, content, organisation and design together form a complete functional text analysis.

tf.questionText: Reading a variety of functional texts, such as recipes and timetables, helps build practical reading skills.
tf.explanation: This matches the genuine, practical value of engaging with diverse functional texts. Exam Tip: Functional texts appear constantly in everyday life, making this a genuinely useful skill.

tf.questionText: Commenting on the usefulness of a functional text means ignoring whether it achieves its intended purpose.
tf.explanation: Commenting on usefulness SPECIFICALLY means assessing whether a text achieves its intended purpose, not ignoring this. Exam Tip: Usefulness evaluation is centred on effectiveness for the intended audience and purpose.

tf.questionText: Composing a functional text, such as a set of instructions, requires considering the intended reader's practical needs.
tf.explanation: This matches the standard, practical approach to composing effective functional texts. Exam Tip: Good functional texts anticipate what the reader actually needs to know or do.

tf.questionText: An application letter's closing should express disinterest in the position.
tf.explanation: An application letter's closing should express GENUINE INTEREST in the position and request further engagement (such as an interview), not disinterest. Exam Tip: The closing is the last impression the letter leaves — it should reinforce enthusiasm for the role.

tf.questionText: A CV is typically organised with clear, structured sections rather than written as a flowing narrative.
tf.explanation: This matches the standard, structured format expected of a CV, distinct from narrative-style writing. Exam Tip: Clear sections (personal details, education, experience, skills) make a CV easy to scan quickly.

tf.questionText: All functional texts share exactly the same format and structure, regardless of their purpose.
tf.explanation: Functional texts VARY WIDELY in format depending on their specific purpose (a recipe looks very different from a CV or brochure); they do not share one fixed format. Exam Tip: Format follows purpose — the structure of a functional text should suit its specific communicative goal.

summary.correctAnswer: A formal letter written to apply for a job vacancy, stating the position applied for, relevant qualifications and requesting further engagement such as an interview.
summary.explanation: It typically opens by naming the position and closes with a polite, positive statement like 'I look forward to the opportunity of an interview.'

summary.correctAnswer: A structured document summarising a person's personal details, education, work experience and skills, submitted alongside a job application.
summary.explanation: Unlike a narrative, a CV is organised into clear sections so an employer can find relevant facts quickly.

summary.correctAnswer: A text written to serve a specific, practical, real-world purpose for a particular audience, such as a CV, brochure, manual or speech.
summary.explanation: Examples include application letters, recipes, timetables and public health posters.

summary.correctAnswer: Examining a functional text's purpose, content, organisation and design to understand how it communicates its message.
summary.explanation: For example, analysing a brochure means asking why it exists, what it says, how it is arranged, and how it looks.

summary.questionText: Reading a variety of functional texts
summary.correctAnswer: Engaging with many different types of practical, purpose-driven texts, such as recipes, timetables, manuals and warranty cards.
summary.explanation: This builds the practical reading skills needed to interpret real-life documents.

summary.questionText: Commenting on the usefulness of a functional text
summary.correctAnswer: Evaluating how effectively a functional text achieves its intended communicative purpose for its intended audience.
summary.explanation: For example, judging whether a bus timetable's departure times are clearly organised and easy to find quickly.

summary.correctAnswer: Creating a new functional text, such as a set of instructions or a brochure, with the intended reader's practical needs clearly in mind.
summary.explanation: A well composed functional text is clear, purposeful and suited to its audience.

summary.correctAnswer: A spoken text prepared for a specific real-world occasion, such as a graduation or wedding, serving a genuine ceremonial or social purpose.
summary.explanation: Because it serves a real purpose and audience, a ceremonial speech counts as a functional text, not mere entertainment.

summary.correctAnswer: The four key dimensions examined when analysing any functional text: why it exists, what it says, how it is arranged, and how it looks.
summary.explanation: Design matters especially for visually-oriented texts like posters and brochures.

summary.correctAnswer: The specific group of readers or listeners a functional text is created for, whose needs shape its content, tone and design.
summary.explanation: A brochure for rural farmers with limited literacy, for instance, may rely more heavily on clear images than text.

hoq.questionText: A student is applying for a part-time job at a local shop and must write BOTH an application letter AND a CV. Explain how the PURPOSE and CONTENT of these two documents should differ, even though they are submitted together.

options.text: Both documents should contain identical content with no distinction

The application letter should be a personalised, persuasive introduction explaining WHY the student is a good fit for this specific role, while the CV should be a structured, factual summary of the student's education, any work experience, and skills, presented clearly for quick reference
The CV should be written as a persuasive letter, and the application letter should be a bare list of facts
Neither document needs any specific structure or purpose

hoq.explanation: The application letter and CV serve complementary but DIFFERENT purposes — the letter persuades and personalises the application for the specific role, while the CV provides an organised, factual reference of qualifications — together they give a complete, professional application package. Exam Tip: Employers often skim the CV for quick facts, then read the letter for personality and motivation — both matter, but differently.

hoq.questionText: A school newspaper club wants to evaluate whether a locally-produced health brochure about malaria prevention is effective for its target audience (rural farmers). Explain the STEPS involved in analysing this functional text and commenting on its usefulness.

options.text: Simply assuming the brochure is effective without any analysis

The club should first analyse the brochure's purpose (informing about malaria prevention), content (accuracy and relevance of the health information), organisation (logical flow of information) and design (use of clear images/colours, given some readers may have limited literacy); then comment on its usefulness by judging how well these elements combine to genuinely inform and persuade the target audience (rural farmers) to take preventive action
Only the brochure's colour scheme matters; content and purpose are irrelevant
The brochure's usefulness cannot be judged without government approval

hoq.explanation: A thorough functional text evaluation requires examining purpose, content, organisation and design TOGETHER, and then judging usefulness specifically in relation to the text's intended audience and goal — a brochure for rural farmers with potentially limited literacy, for example, may need to rely more heavily on clear visuals than a brochure for a more literate audience. Exam Tip: True usefulness evaluation always considers the intended AUDIENCE, not just the text in isolation.

hoq.questionText: A community leader must write BOTH a speech for an upcoming graduation ceremony AND a functional brochure encouraging youth to pursue vocational training. Explain how the WRITING APPROACH should differ between these two functional texts, despite both serving practical, real-world purposes.

options.text: Both texts should be written using identical structure, tone and format

The graduation speech should be spoken aloud, using a warm, celebratory and inspiring tone suited to a live audience, with rhetorical devices to engage listeners in the moment; the brochure should be a written, visually organised document using clear headings, concise persuasive text and supporting images, designed for readers to browse and refer back to at their own pace
The brochure should be delivered orally instead of being written
Functional texts never require any consideration of tone or audience

hoq.explanation: Although both texts serve genuine, practical, real-world communicative purposes, their MEDIUM (spoken vs written/visual) and CONTEXT (a live, emotional ceremony vs a browsable reference document) call for different tones, structures and techniques — recognising this distinction is central to effective functional writing. Exam Tip: Matching a functional text's form to its medium and audience, not just its general purpose, is a genuinely important, exam-relevant writing skill.
